files.label: Game app
files.summary: The Mac app MacNativeGames built for Tears of the Kingdom.
files.detail: Play opens this app. It's named Tears of the Kingdom.app, and MacNativeGames puts it next to your game file unless you chose another folder when building (for example ~/Games/macOS). If a mod changes how much memory the game sets aside, Graft rebuilds this app for you, which takes about a minute.

files.label: Base game
files.summary: Your copy of the game itself: the XCI or NSP file you dumped from your Switch.
files.detail: Graft reads the game's original files from it, so it can combine your mods with them. Reading it needs the keys from your Switch, which you set in Settings.

files.label: Update
files.summary: Your copy of the game's update: the NSP file you dumped from your Switch.
files.detail: Mods are combined with the game files of this exact version, so it has to match the game app's version. You rarely need to choose it yourself: Graft looks inside the update files in your Games folder and picks the one that matches.

files.label: Work folder
files.summary: The folder MacNativeGames worked in when it built the game app.
files.detail: It's named TOTK_build unless you chose another name when building. Graft reads how the game's code is laid out from it, and uses it when it needs to rebuild the app.
